text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Editorial says the state's seizure of millions of dollars deposited in state banks by pyramid scheme companies came too late. The government sequestred money in two banks but none of the big companies have had their funds frozen.

- About 20,000 protestors clashed with police in Vlore after Gjallica scheme company postponed paying back depositors. Angry protestors said Gjallica was one of the main sponsors of the ruling Democratic Party electoral campaign.
- Police arrested 30 investors in the failed Sude pyramid scheme who were believed to be planning a demonstration at Tirana's main Skanderbeg Square.
- The government should take responsibility for the pyramid schemes and intervene immediately, Italian deputy Foreign Minister Piero Fassino said during a one-day visit to Albania.
- Police deactivated a bomb planted at the flat of a prosecutor near a police station in Tirana.

- U.S. assistant State Secretary Timothy Wirth said the Albanian government should have been more careful about the pyramid schemes and repeated his call for a new constitution and the holding of new elections. "Albania is sliding from the road of democracy," he said in a Voice of America interview.
- The editorial says the Socialist Party considers the state and the ruling Democratic Party responsible for the economic crisis caused by the failure of some pyramid schemes.
- The newspaper announces a peaceful protest at Skanderbeg Square on Sunday against the violation of the economic rights of citizens.
